utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, you have now completed your testimony. I would like to thank you, unless Mr. Flynn wanted to add something.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Just one question following up on the president's question, just for clarification, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Mr. Mahmutovic, very briefly, could you tell us if these soldiers died in combat, did they die in combat within the village proper or did they die in combat outside in the trenches, if you know, and how do you know? I mean, do you -- were you present when they were killed? How was it you know that they died in combat?

utterances.speaker: HUSNIJA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: I know about my father because he was very close to me. I know that he was killed there. As for the others who were killed on Bogos, I learned about them from other people, from other combatants.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: All nine others?

utterances.speaker: HUSNIJA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, seven, seven remain. The rest were killed outside the village --

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: Did you witness any of --

utterances.speaker: HUSNIJA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: -- except for Semir Rahic [phoen]. He was killed at the very entrance into the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. FLYNN
utterances.text: And you didn't see any of these deaths occurring, did you?

utterances.speaker: HUSNIJA MAHMUTOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll stop here. Let me sum up so there are no ambiguities. Out of these ten, you said that seven were killed outside the village, seven. And as far as the other three are concerned, the other three on the list, you said that one was killed at the entrance of the village and the two others is mentioned in the transcript. Sir, I'd like to thank you for having come to testify. I wish you a safe journey home, and I would like the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, I hope this will not take too long. I would kindly ask the Trial Chamber to approve the extension of time for the three last submissions by the Prosecutor. We have received one Prosecutor's submission according to Rule 92 bis, for Witness Brix [phoen] Anderson, on the 7th of December 2007, and we will reply within the stipulated term, even before the deadline, towards the end of this week or the beginning of next week. However, on the 10th of December, we received three submissions by the Prosecutor. I must say that they are rather lengthy. The first witness is 92 bis Hasan Rizvic. This is probably not lengthy, but some things have to be checked. There are diverging opinions among the Defence teams. We would like to submit our joint submissions, so it will take us time to agree on the submission. The second is a request to introduce documentary exhibits including the request for the reconsideration, and the third submission is the motion to add two expert opinions to the 65 ter list and also that the documents be admitted into evidence. For this, we will also need time. Your Honours, it is our fondest wish to reply in one joint submission which we will be able to provide very quickly for the first motion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those three motions, one has to do with 92 bis witness. That is not extremely complicated. There is the motion which is a reconsideration motion, which everybody is familiar with because it's the third time that the issue arises. The third motion is the adding on of expert reports on Goranci and DNA. So as you can see, I've had time to scrutinise these three motions. Normally speaking, you had 15 days after the 7th, so 15 plus seven equals 22. So I must just confer with my colleagues to see what extra time we give you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may add to this, we have only received them recently, on the 10th. Two days ago we received the last three. Your Honours, it seems that my microphone was not on. The last three that will take some time to agree on the positions, we only received two days ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber has deliberated, and gives you until the 7th of January for these three motions. You have understood full well that this date was not given out of the blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the registrar to move into private session for a few minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we adjourn, I just wish on behalf of the Defence to wish everyone in the courtroom a good holiday, good rest. You'll need it. We hope to come back next year with more vigour, and we hope to see everybody here after having spent a very good holiday with their families and friends. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, that leaves it incumbent on me. I can't possibly be left out of the good wishes. So all the Judges, to those assisting us in the courtroom and to counsel, I wish them a good holiday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'd like to thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
